cands.bio: U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 4th District since 2023. Earlier worked as an administrator with the Chapel Hill Police Department and at insurance and research companies. Served on the school board (1997-2004), Orange County commissioners (2004-2012), NC House (2013) and NC Senate (2013-2022).

endorsements.text: Endorsed in 2026 by Gov. Josh Stein, Rep. James Clyburn, former Rep. David Price, the Congressional Black Caucus PAC and EMILY's List, per Ballotpedia.
Her campaign site lists endorsements from the Congressional Black Caucus, the Congressional Progressive Caucus, Gov. Josh Stein and former Gov. Roy Cooper.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was raised or when her family's ties to North Carolina began beyond her Chapel Hill birth. We found no stated positions or actions on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on growth or development, school vouchers or teacher pay, or pledges about refusing donor money. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties in the pages reviewed.

workers-first.evidence: Voted Nay on the Laken Riley Act (S.5), which required DHS to detain certain undocumented immigrants arrested for burglary, theft, larceny or shoplifting; it passed the House 263-156 and was signed into law on 1/29/2025.

pro-life.evidence: Sponsored SB 167, the Remove Barriers/Gain Access to Abortion Act, in the North Carolina State Senate (as listed on her 2022 campaign site).

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site says she helped lead the effort to reintroduce the federal assault weapons ban, signed discharge petitions for background-check, bump-stock and other gun bills, and supports bans on high-capacity magazines and local gun buy-back programs.

land-for-floridians.evidence: Her campaign site says she is pushing legislation to stop hedge fund speculators from buying up housing in the district.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says she is a former Chapel Hill Police Department administrator who sponsored a State Senate bill (SB 565, Supporting Law Enforcement) aimed at emphasizing the importance of law enforcement while holding bad actors accountable. The same site also backs ending cash bail and the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act.

cands.name: Mahesh (Max) Ganorkar

money.note: Individuals gave $10,547; PAC money $3,350; candidate's own money $4,569. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for North Carolina's 4th District U.S. House seat in 2026. Holds an MBA. Worked on U.S.–Indian joint ventures and designed homes, then became a stay-at-home father who homeschooled his children. Lost Republican primaries in 2022 and 2024. Has held no elected office.
cands.gaps: We found no record of Ganorkar holding any public office, and no news coverage of his campaigns or conduct. His current campaign website is a "Coming Soon" placeholder, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 or 2024 candidate survey, so we have no 2026 platform from him. The policy statements here come from his 2022 and 2024 campaign websites as quoted by Ballotpedia. We could not find his birth city or the year he moved to North Carolina, so his ties to the state could not be scored. We found no statements from him on data centers, development, growth, homestead property taxes, or foreign or institutional ownership of homes and land. We found no endorsements. His 2022 survey says he was a stay-at-home father and homeschooled his children, but we found no details on his years in business beyond joint ventures and home design.

score.why: Raised $18.6k, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $18.6k, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: MBA; worked on joint ventures between U.S. and Indian companies and in residential home design; later a stay-at-home father and homeschool parent. He founded a Tea Party group in New Jersey in 2009. He has held no public office and lost congressional primaries in 2022 and 2024.
qual.why: He has some business and management background, but the sources give no detail on its scope. He has no legislative, executive, legal or policy-office experience, and his record is thin and self-reported.
qual.label: He has some business and management background, but the sources give no detail on its scope. He has no legislative, executive, legal or policy-office experience, and his record is thin and self-reported.

second-amendment.evidence: Said on his campaign website that he will defend the Second Amendment "without apology or appeasement," and that guns and ammunition should be tax-free and permitting fee-free.

workers-first.evidence: Said on his campaign website that he would fight sanctuary cities, prioritize border security, and make E-Verify mandatory for employment and rental properties, with criminal penalties for violations.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Said on his campaign website that school choice is the answer and that schools should be privatized, with tax dollars allotted to students through parents' tax filings. He did not state a specific teacher pay raise.

pro-life.evidence: Wrote on his campaign website that "we must continue to fight for the unborn." In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey he listed stopping "cultural decay from abortion" among his policy priorities.

back-police-order.evidence: Listed "strong defense and law enforcement" among his policy priorities in his 2022 Ballotpedia survey.

clean-money.evidence: Said on his campaign website that politicians become beholden to dark money and lobbyists, and promised not to add "a dime" to his own balance sheet while in Congress. He did not name specific donors or PACs he would refuse.
